f.title: Address causality, seriousness, frequency, risk factors and misuse in risk assessment
f.statement: Important issues to address in assessing adverse reactions include evidence of causal association, seriousness, absolute and relative frequency, and presence of risk factors that may allow preventive measures; the quality and degree of evidence should be taken into account. Rarely, even a single case report may establish causal association and affect the risk-benefit balance. Risk assessment should also take account of the potential for overdose, misuse, abuse, off-label use and medication errors.

rows.quote: Important issues, which should be addressed in the assessment of adverse reactions, include evidence of causal association, seriousness, absolute and relative frequency and presence of risk factors, which may allow preventive measures.
rows.review_note: Review: three consecutive sentences on the same duty merged; quote proves the lead one. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Propose studies and a new or updated RMP for new safety concerns
f.statement: When new safety concerns are identified that could affect the overall risk-benefit balance, the MAH should propose appropriate studies to further investigate the nature and frequency of the adverse reactions, and propose a new or updated Risk Management Plan accordingly.
f.processes: Risk management & minimisation; Epidemiology / safety studies

rows.quote: When new safety concerns are identified, which, could have an impact on the overall risk-benefit balance of a medicinal product, the MAH should propose appropriate studies to further investigate the nature and frequency of the adverse reactions. A new or updated Risk Management Plan should be proposed accordingly.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Re-evaluate benefit when a new or changing risk is identified
f.statement: When a new or changing risk is identified, the benefit of the medicinal product should be re-evaluated using all available data (e.g. cure or improvement, symptom relief, response rate, duration and quality of life; for prophylactics, reduced severity or incidence; for diagnostics, sensitivity and specificity).

rows.quote: When a new or changing risk is identified, it is important to re-evaluate the benefit of the medicinal product using all available data.
rows.review_note: Review: "it is important" read as Recommended. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Consider misuse and compliance data and quantify benefit
f.statement: Any available information on misuse of the product and the level of compliance in clinical practice that may affect the evaluation of its benefits should be considered; the quality and degree of evidence of benefit should be taken into account, and benefit should as far as possible be expressed quantitatively so it is comparable to the risks.

rows.quote: Any available information on misuse of the product and on the level of compliance in clinical practice, which may have an impact on the evaluation of its benefits, should also be considered.
rows.review_note: Review: the following sentences cross a page break; quote limited to the first. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Optimise safe use and the risk-benefit balance of each product
f.statement: The MAH should aim to optimise the safe use and risk-benefit balance of an individual product and ensure that its adverse effects do not exceed the benefits within the population treated; the balance should be compared with that of other treatments for the same disease. It may be improved by increasing benefits (e.g. restricting use to responders) or reducing risks through risk minimisation measures (contraindications, dose reduction, precautions and warnings, pre-treatment tests, monitoring during treatment).

rows.quote: The MAH should aim to optimize the safe use and the risk-benefit balance of an individual product and ensure that the adverse effects of a medicinal product do not exceed the benefits within the population treated.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Consider feasibility of risk minimisation measures and dose-reduction impact on efficacy
f.statement: When proposing measures to improve the risk-benefit balance, their feasibility in normal conditions of use should be taken into account; if dose reduction is considered as risk minimisation, its impact on efficacy should be carefully evaluated.

rows.quote: When proposing measures to improve the risk-benefit balance of a product, their feasibility in normal conditions of use should be taken into account. If dose reduction is considered as a method of risk minimization, the impact of dose reduction on efficacy should be carefully evaluated.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Initiate urgent safety restrictions and communicate them immediately to TFDA
f.statement: If there are important new safety concerns requiring urgent action, the MAH should initiate urgent safety restrictions, and these measures should be communicated immediately to TFDA.

rows.quote: If there are important new safety concerns requiring urgent action, the MAH, should initiate urgent safety restrictions. These measures should be immediately communicated to TFDA.
rows.review_note: Review: no deadline_rule. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Possible MAH actions: label variation, direct safety communication, withdrawal
f.statement: Actions that may be necessary and may be initiated by the MAH include: variation of the marketing authorisation regarding indication, dosing, contraindications, warnings and precautions, adverse reaction information or other sections of the SPC and PIL; direct provision of important safety information to health care providers, patients and the general public; and withdrawal of the product from the market.

rows.quote: The following types of actions may be necessary and may be initiated by the MAH:
rows.review_note: Review: list summarised. Double-check: "may" = Permitted.

f.title: Establish a PV system with personnel, systems and facilities, subject to TFDA inspection
f.statement: The MAH should establish pharmacovigilance systems. These will be inspected by TFDA (routine and targeted inspections) to ensure compliance with PV requirements; inspections focus on whether the MAH has personnel, systems and facilities in place to meet its regulatory obligations, and are prioritised by risk to public health, nature of products, extent of use, number of products and other risk factors.

rows.quote: The MAH should establish pharmacovigilance systems. Such systems will be inspected by TFDA to ensure compliance with pharmacovigilance requirements.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: confirmed.

f.title: Prepare a remedial action plan for inspection non-compliances
f.statement: Where an inspection reveals non-compliances, the MAH will be required to prepare a remedial action plan to correct the non-compliances and avoid their recurrence.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote: Where an inspection reveals non-compliances the MAH will be required to prepare a remedial action plan to correct the non-compliances and avoid their recurrence.
rows.review_note: Review: no change. Double-check: "will be required" = Mandatory.

f.title: Provide progress reports and evidence on the remedial action plan when required
f.statement: The MAH may be required to provide reports and, where necessary, evidence of the progress and completion of the action plan; there may be re-inspection to verify the progress and success of the remedial actions.
f.processes: Audit & inspection readiness; Quality system & CAPA

rows.quote: The MAH may be required to provide reports and where necessary evidence of the progress and completion of the action plan.

f.title: Non-compliance with PV obligations may lead to TFDA regulatory action
f.statement: In the event of non-compliance, TFDA may take regulatory actions including education and facilitation, re-inspection, a formal warning letter, publishing a list of MAHs found seriously or persistently non-compliant, urgent safety restriction, and variation, suspension or revocation of the marketing authorisation under the Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics Act, No.1, 2003.
f.legal_basis: Tanzania Food, Drugs and Cosmetics Act, No.1, 2003

rows.actor: Tanzania Food and Drugs Authority (action against marketing authorisation holders)

f.title: Seek follow-up on applicable key data elements
f.statement: Some key data elements might not be relevant depending on the circumstances; attempts should be made to obtain follow-up information on as many of the other listed items as are applicable to the case (patient details, suspected product(s), other treatments, reaction details, reporter details, and administrative and MAH details).
f.processes: Case processing & follow-up; ICSR quality control

f.title: Include MAH administrative data and a stable MAH case number in reports
f.statement: Reports should include administrative and MAH details: source of report (e.g. spontaneous, literature), date the report was first received by the MAH, country of occurrence, type (initial or follow-up) and sequence of case information reported to TFDA, name and address of the MAH, contact details of the MAH contact person, and the MAH identification number for the case; the same number should be used for the initial and follow-up reports on the same case.

f.title: Alternative approaches acceptable with adequate justification
f.statement: The guidelines allow flexibility: alternative approaches to the principles and practices described may be acceptable provided they are supported by adequate justification and meet the minimum recommended ADR reporting requirements. TFDA reserves the right to request information or material, or define conditions not described in the guidelines, to assess safety, efficacy or quality.
f.exceptions: Clinical-trial adverse events (Sections 61 to 72 of the Act) are outside the scope of the guidelines
